styleReferenceRole: 2D illustration style only; the protagonist is not renamed as these civilians

genderPolicy: Only explicit source family roles establish a gender. Unspecified source genders remain unspecified in the manifest; practical androgynous costume/face design is a visual interpretation.
agePolicy: Source ages and elapsed years determine the eight age pairs. Approximate numeric ages inferred only for a child/teen drawing are labelled as visual estimates.

generationHistory.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: production transparent PNG portrait atlas for a Korean historical visual novel, sheet 1 of 2.
Input image 1 is ONLY an approved illustration STYLE reference. Borrow its fine dark linework, softly shaded 2D painted-cel finish, believable faces and muted cloth colors. Do not copy the heroine's face or costume.
Make ONE square high-resolution sheet, ideally 2048 x 2048, with an EXACT invisible 4-column by 4-row uniform grid. Each cell is exactly one quarter of the total width and height. Fifteen separate characters, one centered in each specified cell, and the final bottom-right cell entirely empty transparent. All canvas outside character silhouettes must be genuinely transparent alpha, including gutters and the empty cell. No visible checkerboard, backgrounds, plates, colored rectangles, shadows behind people, lettering, labels, numbers, borders or grid lines.
Framing: each character is a large waist-up portrait, head fully included, torso cut neatly at the waist within the cell; top of hair around 6% below its cell top, waist around 94%, shoulders comfortably inside 90% cell width. Leave a transparent gutter inside every cell edge. No portrait may cross a cell boundary. All face gently toward the viewer with a slight turn to the viewer's RIGHT (toward the heroine's UI slot), calm attentive neutral expressions. Do not render hands or held objects. Practical ancient Korean commoner robes appropriate to each specified era; no crowns, court regalia, modern fashion, armor, fantasy weapons, ornate Joseon court hats or sexualized clothes.
Use DISTINCT adult faces and hair arrangements. Characters whose gender is unspecified must have natural androgynous facial features and plain practical clothing, not exaggerated gender presentation. These are fictional civilians, not purported historical likenesses.

The following row/column positions are ONE-BASED instructions only, never printed:
ROW 1, COLUMN 1: Yeonwoo / 연우, adult Goguryeo farmer in 194; gender unspecified. Long oval face, straight brows, dark hair tied low, plain sage outer robe over oatmeal tunic, subtle work-worn cloth. Responsible and worried but neutral.
ROW 1, COLUMN 2: Mojin / 모진, adult Goguryeo granary keeper in 194; gender unspecified. Broader round face, small attentive eyes, loosely tied hair beneath a plain dark brown cloth band, brown-grey practical jacket. Distinct from Yeonwoo.
ROW 1, COLUMN 3: Dorim / 도림, adult Goguryeo frontier gate worker in the early 4th century; gender unspecified. Angular cheekbones, close neat tied hair, dark slate wrap coat with a rust collar, alert neutral face.
ROW 1, COLUMN 4: Soun / 소운, adult displaced Goguryeo returnee in the 4th century; gender unspecified. Soft square face, gently hooded eyes, loosely swept dark hair, faded ochre robe and simple cream shoulder wrap.

ROW 2, COLUMN 1: Daeun / 다은, adult Goguryeo migrant leaving home in 427; gender unspecified. Slender long face, soft straight eyebrows, long black hair bundled at the nape, muted plum-brown robe and light tan collar. This is the 427 character, not a similarly named descendant in another chapter.
ROW 2, COLUMN 2: Yunseo / 윤서, adult civilian resident of Ansi fortress in 645; gender unspecified. Compact sturdy build, rounded nose, tied dark hair with a plain blue head cloth, muted blue-grey working robe with cream undersleeves.
ROW 2, COLUMN 3: Taemun / 태문, adult MALE refugee father in 668; medium build, slightly long nose, short restrained moustache and stubble, black hair tied back, worn brown outer robe over a pale moss tunic. Concerned but composed.
ROW 2, COLUMN 4: Haein / 해인, INITIAL age in the 20s in 475, Baekje refugee who repairs and trades household goods; gender unspecified. Distinct narrow oval face, almond eyes, a few loose strands at the temples, black hair tied in a low short tail. Muted brick-red collar and teal-grey work jacket. This exact facial identity returns in ROW 3 COLUMN 1.

ROW 3, COLUMN 1: Haein / 해인, SAME person as ROW 2 COLUMN 4, now in their 40s around 492-495. Preserve face shape, eyes, eyebrows, nose, mouth and hairline. Add believable subtle age lines around eyes and a slightly weathered face, a few grey strands; do not make elderly. Similar teal-grey jacket with brick-red collar.
ROW 3, COLUMN 2: Yeoul / 여울, INITIAL age in the 20s in 510, Baekje local administrative clerk; gender unspecified. Wider oval face, long fine straight brows, neat center-part dark hair tied behind, plain dusty-indigo collar and light taupe robe. Same person returns next cell.
ROW 3, COLUMN 3: Yeoul / 여울, SAME person as ROW 3 COLUMN 2, now in late 60s in 554; preserve recognizable bone structure and eyes, naturally grey hair, wrinkles and slightly leaner cheeks. Similar taupe robe with dusty-indigo collar. This is the grandparent of a soldier, not that soldier.
ROW 3, COLUMN 4: Ara / 아라, Gaya merchant in their 20s in the third century; gender unspecified. Round-oval face, bright alert eyes, wavy black hair loosely knotted, warm terracotta work coat with cream collar. This is the third-century Ara, not the different Ara of 532 or another century.

ROW 4, COLUMN 1: Haedeul / 해들, Gaya ironworker, adult of the same generation as the third-century Ara; gender unspecified. Broad angular face, strong but not exaggerated physique, tied-back hair with simple dark cloth headband, plain charcoal work apron over muted warm-grey long-sleeved robe. No held tools.
ROW 4, COLUMN 2: Bora / 보라, adult Silla village neighbor in the seventh century; gender unspecified. Round kind face, slightly arched brows, dark hair tied loosely with an ochre strip, dusty mustard outer robe and moss collar. Natural unembellished village clothing.
ROW 4, COLUMN 3: Haemyeong / 해명, Silla stonemason around age 30 in 751; gender unspecified. Lean square face, narrow eyes, cropped side wisps with tied top hair, faded stone-blue work robe and plain beige shoulder cloth. Keep hands out of frame: do not depict an injury, cast or bandage because the portrait must work before and after a story event.
ROW 4, COLUMN 4: EMPTY, entirely transparent, no person or object.

Consistency constraints: Haein's two ages must clearly be one individual; Yeoul's two ages must clearly be one different individual. Every other person must have their own face rather than clones. Render all 15 portraits with equally polished detail and consistent proportions and lighting. No text anywhere. True alpha transparency. Exact 4x4 uniform sprite atlas.

Use case: identity-preserve.
Edit this transparent 15-portrait character atlas ONLY to correct its uniform sprite-cell layout.
Keep all fifteen portraits, their current order, identity, faces, ages, costumes, linework and soft 2D rendering. Keep the last bottom-right cell empty. Keep genuine alpha transparency.
The output must remain a SQUARE 4 by 4 equal-cell atlas. Reposition and REDUCE each complete portrait enough to leave at least 8% OF ITS CELL HEIGHT of fully transparent margin above the hair AND below its flat torso cutoff, and at least 5% OF ITS CELL WIDTH on both sides. Each full character silhouette must stay entirely in its own equal-size cell. Important: the existing third row begins too high and collides with the second row's exact boundary. All row starts must match the mathematical quarters of the full square canvas. Center every bust within its proper cell. Do not resize the whole grid while leaving its contents overflowing. Do not create guide lines, text, borders, panels or background color.
Uniform grid: row1 has four people; row2 four people; row3 four people; row4 three people then one empty cell. Exactly fifteen. Match original face identities and clear aging of the paired Haein (row2 col4 and row3 col1) and Yeoul (row3 col2 and col3). Use the high resolution necessary for game portraits. Do not change direction or introduce new accessories.

Use case: identity-preserve.
Technical cleanup of the supplied transparent character sprite atlas. Preserve every face, costume, age, identity and cell order. This is NOT a redesign.
Reflow the existing busts into a mathematically UNIFORM 4-column by 4-row square grid with LARGE CLEAR TRANSPARENT GUTTERS. The current portraits touch row and column boundaries, so they will bleed when clipped by CSS; fix that.
MANDATORY: leave a continuous transparent horizontal band, about 4% of the total canvas height thick, centered at exactly 25%, 50% and 75% of the canvas height. Also leave transparent vertical bands 3% of the total canvas width thick centered at exactly 25%, 50% and 75% of canvas width. These bands must run clear across the whole sheet with absolutely no character pixels. Leave transparent outside margins. Shrink and center each COMPLETE portrait to fit the remaining rectangular area inside its original cell, keeping all of the head and the shoulders. Repaint/reposition complete heads rather than cropping them at the bands. Each bust should still fill most of its remaining cell interior and be crisp enough for game UI. The empty bottom-right cells remain entirely empty; do not add portraits there.
No actual visible bands, lines or panels: the gutters are empty ALPHA transparency. Keep the background and blank cells genuinely transparent. Clean isolated bright red/yellow fringe pixels around silhouettes. NO letters, captions, numbers, labels, watermarks or checkerboard. Keep all portraits in the same 2D illustration style and their existing facing direction.
